thread:
Jen: Heads up — I pulled a heap profile from the canary that hit OOMs this morning. Looks like the kernel routing change picks a larger 'packed-kernel' for mixed-length batches and we blow the workspace on GPUs with lots of KV fragments. :confused:
Sam: ugh. any quick logs/snips?
Jen: pasted the profiler snippet below (truncated):
```
GPU 0 workspace_used=1.9G workspace_alloc=2.1G
KV cache fragments_total=482 fragments_avg=3.8 prefill_bytes=512MB decode_bytes=1.4GB
kernel_selected=packed-kernel-v2 (expected: streaming-kernel)
batch_shapes=[{seq:8},{seq:384},{seq:64}]
```
Marta: that routing table change we merged last week prioritized kernel throughput for median seq len. mixed batches with a long tail will push packed kernels. We should have a safety guard.
Ryan: likely fragmentation + large kernel working set = alloc failure. Can we force decode-path for mixed shapes?
Sam: quick mitigation proposal: set per-request soft cap on workspace to 700MB (env var: WORKSPACE_SOFT_CAP=0.7) and fallback kernel to streaming-kernel when any seq > 256. low-risk config change.
Jen: I ran a smoke with WORKSPACE_SOFT_CAP=0.7 locally — no OOMs on the failing traces, p95 latency +3% but throughput same. raw numbers: baseline p95=78ms -> 80ms, p99 spikes removed.
Marta: +1 for quick rollback-ish config. longer term we should adapt kernel scoring to include estimated fragmentation cost (prefill vs decode). current score = f(hardware, seq_mean), need f += frag_penalty.
Ekaterina: can someone add a cheap estimator for frag_penalty: frag_penalty = alpha * fragments_total / slots_free. alpha tuned to match sim. That should push routing away from packed-kernel when we know memory is fragmented.
Sam: I'll open a small PR to add the WORKSPACE_SOFT_CAP default to 0.7 in canary and add the streaming-kernel fallback rule for seq > 256. Also adding a opt-in flag to enable the frag_penalty calcs later.
OpsBot: deploy started: canary/pm-slice -> 3 hosts. rollout ETA ~15m. CI checks passed. :rocket:
Jen: thx. also adding an alloc debug flag to collect per-request slab usage so we can validate frag_penalty numbers: export ALLOC_DEBUG=1 (sends events to /telemetry/allocs).
Ryan: for eviction heuristics: recommendation from sim — when prefill_bytes > decode_bytes and fragments_total high, prefer decode-only eviction (don't prefill) for that request. avoids creating many small slabs. set REQUEST_PREFILL_THRESHOLD=0.6 (prefill if prefill/total > 0.6).
Marta: good idea. that decouples prefill aggressiveness from global policy. add it as a per-route override so we can target routes with long-tail sequences.
Ekaterina: I'll run a quick sim tomorrow with alpha in {0.4,0.7,1.0} and REQUEST_PREFILL_THRESHOLD in {0.5,0.6,0.8} and post heatmaps. If the frag_penalty correlates with reduced OOMs we can bake it into kernel scoring.
Jen: plan: 1) Sam deploys soft cap + fallback (canary) 2) Ops validates no OOMs and sanity metrics (workspace_alloc, slab_count) 3) Ekaterina runs sims and feeds alpha back 4) Marta/Infra update routing score and add per-route prefill override 5) release to prod after 48h canary.
Sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4892 (draft). added envs and fallback rule + minimal telemetry.
Jen: thanks — keeping thread open. if canary still sees OOMs I'll revert kernel routing change. :eyes:
